purpose: Add Low-Quality Image Placeholder (LQIP) and Dominant Color placeholder support for lazy-loaded images, replacing the hardcoded gray SVG with three user-selectable placeholder types (SVG colored by dominant color, Dominant Color, and LQIP blurred preview).
riskRationale: All critical and data-loss bugs from earlier review iterations have been fixed (commit_img_info() concurrent merge bug, missing SCSS file, missing IntersectionObserver fallback, missing WebP/GIF extraction). The implementation follows the existing deferred-commit pattern and builds on well-tested infrastructure. The remaining important concern is architectural (in-memory overhead of loading the full wppo_img_info option on every front-end page when LQIP/dominant color is active), which has meaningful performance implications for large media libraries but does not cause incorrect behavior or data loss.
breakingChanges: Private method post_process_svg_placeholders() renamed to post_process_placeholders() with changed signature
replacePlaceholderWithSVG boolean setting replaced with placeholderType string (backward-compat migration included)

text: The PR is well-architected with clean separation between placeholder extraction (Img_Converter) and application (Image_Optimisation), proper backward-compatibility for the old setting, and smooth frontend transitions. 13 of 14 issues from earlier review rounds have been fixed, including the critical concurrent data-loss bug in commit_img_info(), missing IntersectionObserver fallback, WebP/GIF placeholder extraction, attachment deletion cleanup, transparency handling, and LQIP height capping. One important architectural concern (memory overhead of loading the full wppo_img_info option on every page view) and one minor cleanup issue (orphaned resized-image placeholder entries) remain.

reasoning: One important architectural concern persists: get_placeholder_src_for_image() loads the entire wppo_img_info option (potentially hundreds of KB) into memory on every front-end page view when dominant_color or lqip placeholder types are active. While the functionality is correct and all critical/data-loss bugs are fixed, this has meaningful performance implications for sites with large media libraries that should be addressed before merge.

message: Clean backward-compatibility migration from replacePlaceholderWithSVG to placeholderType with proper ternary fallback chains for existing saved settings.
Dominant color extraction uses reduced-stride pixel sampling, balancing accuracy against performance with reasonable defaults.
commit_img_info() now merges dominant_color and lqip arrays atomically alongside status arrays, preventing concurrent data loss between parallel conversion requests.
Dominant-color placeholder uses a transparent 1x1 SVG data URI with CSS background-color, providing a visible fade transition on image load.
Placeholder extraction is called for WebP and GIF source images before early returns, ensuring all source formats get placeholder entries.
The scroll-based IntersectionObserver fallback applies dominant-color background, LQIP blur class, and self-removing load event listeners, matching the IntersectionObserver path.
delete_attachment hook correctly registered for pruning orphaned placeholder entries on image deletion.

get_placeholder_src_for_image() loads the entire wppo_img_info option via Img_Converter::get_img_info() on every front-end page view when dominant_color or lqip placeholder is active. This option aggregates all converted-image metadata (dominant colors, LQIP data URIs, conversion status for every format) and can grow to hundreds of KB for large media libraries. While statically cached per-request, the initial deserialization cost and memory overhead are paid on every page load. Previously reported in earlier review rounds but not addressed.
suggestion: Store dominant_color and lqip data in a separate, slimmer option keyed only by relative path, queried by targeted lookup rather than loading the entire blob. Alternatively, implement a custom DB table for placeholder lookups. At minimum, document the memory impact in AGENTS.md for operators of large media libraries.

message: clean_placeholder_on_delete() only removes placeholder entries for the main attachment file. WordPress generates multiple resized versions per upload (e.g. image-150x150.jpg, image-300x200.jpg), and each may have its own entry in wppo_img_info['dominant_color'] and wppo_img_info['lqip']. These orphaned entries accumulate over time as attachments are deleted, contributing to unbounded growth of the option.
suggestion: After cleaning the main file's entries, iterate over wp_get_attachment_metadata()['sizes'] to get all resized filenames in the same directory and remove their placeholder entries too, using the directory of the main file and each resized filename to compute relative paths for cleanup.
